groups.text: It is currently 18 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Iran has announced funeral ceremonies for its late Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, running from July 3 to 9 and ending with a burial at the Imam Reza Shrine in Mashhad. The event follows a four-month delay caused by conflicts involving Israel and the United States, leaving an interim council to manage a constitutional transition until the Assembly of Experts elects a new leader. In Europe, the crypto exchange Binance has suspended services for new users in Spain, Italy, France, and Poland. This follows the exchange's withdrawal of its MiCA license application from Greece just before the July 1 enforcement deadline. Binance argues that the success of the EU regulatory framework depends on licensed entities rather than exclusions. Meanwhile, enterprises are focusing on AI inference to gain a competitive edge. Success now depends on how many workloads and users an infrastructure can serve without increasing costs or sacrificing performance.

Lithuania is moving to lift its ban on hosting nuclear weapons. President Gitanas Nauseda says political party leaders have agreed in principle to amend or remove Article 137 of the constitution, which currently forbids foreign military bases and weapons of mass destruction. Nauseda argues that the law is obsolete and warns that Lithuania cannot afford to be a grey zone or a weak link within NATO. The country already spends four percent of its GDP on defense and hosts a NATO multinational battlegroup. Meanwhile, extreme heat is straining European infrastructure. Temperatures hit 40 degrees Celsius across Poland, Germany, and the Czech Republic this past Sunday, causing transport systems to buckle. In France, spikes up to 44 degrees Celsius followed by storms left an estimated one thousand excess deaths. Separately, in software development, a new PyTorch pull request aims to refine power handles via pyzes 0.1.2 while maintaining compatibility with version 0.1.1.

In Venezuela, Acting President Delcy Rodríguez has called Hernán Gil a living miracle after emergency workers pulled him from under 140 tonnes of rubble eight days after twin earthquakes hit on June 24th. While rescue teams spent over 100 hours freeing Gil from a collapsed car park, the death toll from the quakes has reached 2,595 people with tens of thousands still missing. Rodríguez rejected claims that her government reacted too slowly to the tragedy. In Ukraine, Russian forces carried out nearly 110 attacks on populated areas in the Sumy region over the last twenty-four hours, killing five people and injuring 34 others using drones, artillery, and guided bombs. Meanwhile, Julian Nagelsmann is stepping down as Germany's national football coach following a premature World Cup exit against Paraguay. The DFB expects Jürgen Klopp to take over, while Nagelsmann will reportedly receive one year's salary as a severance payment.

Bitcoin holders are facing a significant downturn as more of the currency is now held at a loss than at a profit. Glassnode data shows roughly 10.83 million BTC are currently underwater, reflecting a deep correction from the January peak of 109,000 dollars. While Bitcoin traded around 61,361 dollars on Thursday, Animoca Brands is betting on a different future for blockchain infrastructure. Co-founder Yat Siu envisions an agentic economy where 50 to 200 billion autonomous AI agents require on-chain wallets by 2031. To support this, the company launched the Animoca Minds platform in February and earmarked 10 million dollars for developers in May. This push for digital automation contrasts with immediate geopolitical instability in the Middle East. Iranian commander Ali Abdollahi has warned the U.S. and Israel against military action during the funeral of former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, a situation that market pricing suggests may actually decrease the likelihood of the regime falling before 2027.

Berlin police are preparing to launch a new behavior-scanning software this quarter at Kottbusser Tor. The system uses specialized cameras to automatically analyze pedestrians, categorizing their actions as either irrelevant or problematic to detect emergency situations. While police have completed the validation tests, Vasili Franco of the Green Party calls the plan madness, citing studies that suggest surveillance merely displaces crime rather than stopping it. In a separate matter of digital security, nineteen-year-old Peter Stokes has been extradited to the United States from Finland. A dual US-Estonian national and member of the Scattered Spider hacking collective, Stokes faces federal charges for his alleged role in a May 2025 breach of a luxury jewelry retailer. The attackers demanded eight million dollars in cryptocurrency, but the company refused to pay, spending over two million dollars instead to recover its systems from the attack.

PyTorch developers are moving to make the framework more device-generic, reducing its reliance on specific hardware. In one update, engineers removed unnecessary CUDA restrictions from three optimizer tests so they can run on CPUs and future backends like XPU or MPS. Another fix replaces hardcoded CUDA checks in inductor logging paths with a general GPU helper to better support non-CUDA hardware. These technical shifts contrast with the hurdles facing those trying to enter the field from the outside. On Reddit, a high school student seeking a path into machine learning expressed frustration while self-studying calculus. The student is currently using Stewart's Calculus but is questioning if Spivak's Calculus would be a better choice for their education. While professional developers refine the software to work across more devices, new students are still struggling to find the right foundational guidance to begin.

A man has died after setting himself on fire outside the United Nations headquarters in New York. Police responded to the emergency call around 6:30 p.m., transporting the fifty-two-year-old man to Bellevue Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. While authorities have not confirmed a motive, activists and the International Campaign for Tibet identified him as Lobga Rangzen, an Uber driver and advocate for Tibetan independence from China. In sports, Portugal has advanced to the World Cup round of sixteen after a dramatic two-to-one victory over Croatia, secured by a stoppage-time goal from Gonçalo Ramos and a penalty from Cristiano Ronaldo; they will next face Spain. Meanwhile, as the United States marks its 250th anniversary of independence, historians are reflecting on how King Louis XVI supported the American Revolutionaries to weaken his British rivals.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 20 and 22 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your work calendar has a NAS brainstorm at one in the afternoon and beer and cocktails at five in the evening. Your personal calendar has Höfische at seven in the evening.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
